mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM < -1.0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation above 4% (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy pivot toward easing amid high inflation, which historically has been associated with positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates fall.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 104.0 (i.e., >4%) in the same month
regime_hint: policy pivot from tightening to easing
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 1% for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS MoM > 1.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) month-over-month indicates a compositional shift toward lower-wage employment, which reduces average labor productivity and drags on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a sustained manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings for industrial firms and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM > 0.5% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
